A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ONC study, with matching CLM/UFM formulations and core theorems. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical solutions of the equations of state and neural-network experiments on five ordinal datasets, including training curves and feature visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds UTKFace experiments, clog-log experiments and a direct comparison between theoretical predictions and trained networks.

M1.justification: The central CLM/UFM formulation and threshold parameterization remain unchanged. However, Appendix D.5 explicitly adds feature-norm regularization to the DNN training objective for the new theory-validation experiment; this is a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds face-image age estimation on UTKFace, grouped into 20 ordinal classes, extending evaluation beyond the five retained tabular ordinal datasets. This introduces a substantially different input domain and prediction task.

E2.justification: Fixed and learnable thresholds remain the comparison pair in corresponding experiments. No external ordinal-regression baseline is added or removed; additional backbones and link functions are experimental configurations within the existing framework.

E3.justification: v2 adds accuracy, QWK, within-1 accuracy and minimum sensitivity, plus an adjusted ONC3 metric for fixed-threshold clog-log experiments. New UTKFace protocols specify an 80/20 stratified split, image preprocessing, three pretrained backbones and 300-epoch training. Appendix D.5 adds a 35-value regularization sweep. Existing tabular training settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 newly tests whether ONC extends to an asymmetric link function. Appendix D.4 examines consistency across image backbones, and D.5 directly tests EOS predictions against trained networks across regularization strengths. The last analysis reveals quantitative discrepancies that v1's numerical EOS illustration did not examine.

E5.justification: v1 already uses 30-holdout averaging and shaded uncertainty bands. v2 adds three-seed repetitions for UTKFace, documents their averaged error bands, and reports error bars for the EOS–network comparison. The precise statistical definition of the bands remains unspecified.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for UTKFace, clog-log configurations and additional metrics on retained datasets. Figures 3, 35 and 36 report zero minimum sensitivity for learnable thresholds across all three image backbones, versus positive values for fixed thresholds. Figure 39 newly shows network weight-norm saturation and transition points differing from EOS predictions. These are new findings under added or modified settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces v1's CDF-difference strict-log-concavity argument with a multidimensional translated-integral theorem, a geometric assumption and six supporting lemmas. Appendix D.3 also derives the asymmetric-link offset and defines an adjusted ONC3 metric. The main ONC and EOS theorem statements are largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and central theoretical contributions remain essentially unchanged. The conclusion expands the demonstrated practical benefit of fixed thresholds from faster, more stable training to better classification accuracy, reflecting the new image experiments.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces the speculative minority-class benefit with an interpretation of UTKFace results and narrows its learnable-threshold discussion to ONC1–2. It newly acknowledges that the existing ONC3 metric requires uniformly spaced fixed thresholds. Appendix D.5 explicitly limits the theory's agreement with real networks to qualitative behavior in important respects.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds image preprocessing, pretrained-backbone adaptations, architecture-specific hyperparameters, distributed training details and runtime information; Table 3 adds clog-log settings. The new checklist also reports supplementary code and run instructions, specifically identifying tabular logit/probit code. Actual supplementary-code availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Leindler, Brøndsted and UTKFace/ResNet/DenseNet references, while removing the Barbato and Brascamp–Lieb proof sources. Section 2 revises its description of linguistic collapse, but the overall positioning within neural-collapse research remains stable.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and main section sequence are retained, with much introductory and formulation prose unchanged. Editing concentrates on experimental descriptions, discussion, conclusion and the revised mathematical appendix. v2 also condenses affiliations and adds acknowledgments and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: Existing six-panel metric figures become ten-panel displays, with reordered panels and logarithmic MAE axes. v2 adds UTKFace, clog-log and theory-comparison figures, expands the hyperparameter table and adds two UTKFace tables. The old strict-log-concavity diagram is removed with its replaced proof.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly could not evaluate the hypothesized minority-class benefit because its datasets yielded near-zero validation error. v2 addresses this limitation with a harder image task across three backbones and adds a direct theory–network comparison that exposes quantitative failures. These targeted checks substantially strengthen the empirical grounding and clarify applicability. The learnable-threshold ONC3 metric remains unresolved, and label-shift robustness is still not directly tested, but the expanded validation and more candid limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
